subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the direction cosines of two lines which are connected by the relations l−5m+3n=0 and 7l²+5m²−3n²=0.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what separates direction ratios from direction cosines.

steps.label: Write the two relations
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two relations are given, one linear and one of second degree. Make one letter the subject of the LINEAR one — it is always the easier to rearrange.
steps.memory_tip: Make one letter the subject of the linear relation before substituting anywhere.

recall.must_convey: That the linear relation is rearranged to make one letter the subject.
accept: make one letter the subject of the linear relation
rearrange the first equation and substitute into the second
the linear one is easier to rearrange
linear equation nunchi oka letter ni subject cheyyali
write both relations and rearrange the first

steps.why: Two relations connect three unknowns, so the pair fixes only the RATIO l : m : n — which is all a direction needs. Eliminating one letter turns the pair into a single quadratic, and its two roots are the two lines.
common_mistakes: Rearranging the second-degree relation instead, which needs a square root.
Sign slip when moving a term across.

steps.label: Eliminate and factorise
steps.margin_note: Three marks. Substituting leaves one homogeneous quadratic in two letters. It always factors, and each factor is one of the two lines.
steps.memory_tip: One homogeneous quadratic comes out, and it factors into the two lines.

recall.must_convey: That substituting gives a homogeneous quadratic which factorises into two cases.
accept: substitute into the second relation to get a quadratic then factorise it
the quadratic factors into two brackets, one for each line
each factor gives one of the two lines
substitute chesthe quadratic vasthundi, factorise cheyyali
this gives the two cases

steps.why: The quadratic is homogeneous, so it factors into two linear pieces — which is exactly why there are TWO lines rather than one. The problem is a pair from the start.
common_mistakes: Trying to solve for numerical values of l, m, n rather than a ratio.
Missing one of the two factors and finding only one line.

steps.label: Case (i): the first line
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Take the first factor, feed it back into the linear relation, and read off the ratio l : m : n. Clearing the common letter leaves whole numbers.
steps.memory_tip: Feed the first factor back and read off the ratio l : m : n.
lines: So, d.r's of L₁ = (a₁, b₁, c₁) = (1, 2, 3)  ……(3)

recall.must_convey: That the first factor gives a ratio l : m : n and hence the first line's direction ratios.
accept: put the first factor back into the linear relation and read off the ratio
cancel the common letter to get whole numbers
this gives the direction ratios of the first line
modati case nunchi ratio teesukovali
the first line's d r's

steps.why: Only the RATIO matters, so any common factor may be cancelled — which is what turns fractions into the small whole numbers the answer carries.
common_mistakes: Keeping the common letter and carrying fractions forward.
Reading the ratio in the wrong order.

steps.label: Case (ii): the second line
steps.margin_note: Two marks. The same work on the second factor. The two lines the question asks about are these two.
steps.memory_tip: The same on the second factor.
lines: Case (ii): Put m = n/2 in (1), then
So, d.r's of L₂ = (a₂, b₂, c₂) = (−1, 1, 2)  ……(4)

recall.must_convey: That the second factor gives the second line's direction ratios the same way.
accept: do the same with the second factor
put the second root back and read off the ratio
this gives the second line's direction ratios
rendo case ni kooda same ga cheyyali
the second line's d r's

steps.why: Both factors have to be used — the question asks about TWO lines, and stopping at one answers half of it.
common_mistakes: Reusing the first factor by mistake.
Sign slip that makes the second line identical to the first.

steps.label: Find the direction cosines
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Direction ratios are enough to fix a direction, but the question asks for direction COSINES — so each triple is divided by the square root of the sum of its squares.
steps.memory_tip: The question asks for direction COSINES, so divide each triple by the root of its sum of squares.

recall.must_convey: That each triple is divided by the root of the sum of its squares to give the direction cosines.
accept: divide each triple by the root of the sum of the squares
direction cosines are the ratios normalised
divide by root l squared plus m squared plus n squared
root of sum of squares tho divide cheyyali
these are the direction cosines
heard_as: root of the sum of squares

steps.why: Direction ratios give the direction; direction cosines are that same direction scaled so the squares add to 1. Dividing by √(a²+b²+c²) is the only step between them.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to divide one of the two triples.
Dropping the ± that both directions along a line allow.
